title: Finite-presentation modules on a ringed space have a set of isomorphism representatives
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Say that $\mathcal G\in\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation if every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ admitting an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ with $m,n$ finite [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Then there are a set $I$ and finite-presentation modules $(\mathcal G_i)_{i\in I}$ such that every finite-presentation $\mathcal O_X$-module is isomorphic to some $\mathcal G_i$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), lines 957-984; apply it because a module of finite presentation is of finite type by Modules, Definition 01BN

proof.text: Two facts from the definitions [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. (i) A module $\mathcal G$ of finite presentation is of finite type: given $x$, an open $U\ni x$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal G|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n})$, the composite of the cokernel map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha)$ (an epimorphism) with this isomorphism is an epimorphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$, which is of the form $e_i\mapsto s_i$ for the sections $s_i\in\mathcal G(U)$ that are the images of the $e_i$. (ii) Finite presentation is invariant under isomorphism: if $\mathcal G\cong\mathcal G'$ and $\mathcal G'$ is of finite presentation, restrict the isomorphism to the open $U$ of a local presentation of $\mathcal G'|_U$ and compose.

source.place: Modules, Definition 01B5 (definition-finite-type, line 810) and Definition 01BN (definition-finite-presentation, line 1378)

proof.text: The set of data. For an open $U\subseteq X$ write $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$; $(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is a ringed space, so $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is an abelian category in which kernels are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $T$ be the collection of triples $(U,r,\mathcal K)$ with $U\subseteq X$ open, $r\ge0$ an integer and $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ a sub-$\mathcal O_U$-module, i.e. a family of submodules $\mathcal K(W)\subseteq\mathcal O_X(W)^{\oplus r}$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) stable under restriction and forming a sheaf. $T$ is a set: it is a subset of $\mathcal P(\operatorname{Op}(X))\times\mathbb N\times\prod_{W\in\operatorname{Op}(X)}\mathcal P(\mathcal O_X(W)^{\oplus r})$ (over each $r$). Using the axiom of choice, fix for each $t=(U,r,\mathcal K)\in T$ a cokernel $\pi_t:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to Q_t$ of the inclusion $\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ (it exists since $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is abelian). Let $D$ be the collection of tuples $d=(\mathcal U,(r_U,\mathcal K_U)_{U\in\mathcal U},(\varphi_{UV})_{U,V\in\mathcal U})$ where $\mathcal U\subseteq\operatorname{Op}(X)$ is a set of opens covering $X$ (the covering indexed by itself, as Stacks indexes it by an injection $J\to\mathcal P(X)$), $t_U=(U,r_U,\mathcal K_U)\in T$, and $\varphi_{UV}:Q_{t_U}|_{U\cap V}\to Q_{t_V}|_{U\cap V}$ are $\mathcal O_{U\cap V}$-linear isomorphisms satisfying the cocycle condition $\varphi_{UW}=\varphi_{VW}\circ\varphi_{UV}$ on $U\cap V\cap W$. $D$ is a set: a morphism $Q|_{U\cap V}\to Q'|_{U\cap V}$ is a family of maps $Q(W)\to Q'(W)$ ($W\subseteq U\cap V$ open), an element of the set $\prod_W\operatorname{Map}(Q(W),Q'(W))$, so $D$ is a subset of $\coprod_{\mathcal U}\prod_{U\in\mathcal U}T\times\prod_{U,V\in\mathcal U}\prod_W\operatorname{Map}(Q_{t_U}(W),Q_{t_V}(W))$, built from sets by products, power sets and disjoint unions indexed by sets.

Glueing. For each $d\in D$ the modules $Q_{t_U}$ ($U\in\mathcal U$) on the covering $X=\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal U}U$ with the isomorphisms $\varphi_{UV}$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (2), which gives an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $\mathcal O_U$-linear isomorphisms $\theta_U$ from its restriction to $U$ onto $Q_{t_U}$ with $\varphi_{UV}\circ\theta_U|_{U\cap V}=\theta_V|_{U\cap V}$. By choice (over the set $D$) fix one such module $\Phi(d)$ with isomorphisms $\theta^d_U:\Phi(d)|_U\to Q_{t_U}$. Then $\{\Phi(d):d\in D\}$ is a set of $\mathcal O_X$-modules indexed by $D$.

source.place: Sheaves, Section 00AK (section-glueing-sheaves), Lemmas 00AL, 00AM; used in Modules, Lemma 01BC, proof, lines 976-981

proof.text: A datum for a finite type module. Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For each $x\in X$ there are an open $U_x\ni x$, an integer $n_x$ and an epimorphism $\mathcal O_{U_x}^{\oplus n_x}\to\mathcal F|_{U_x}$. Let $\mathcal U=\{U_x:x\in X\}\subseteq\operatorname{Op}(X)$, a set of opens covering $X$, and for each $U\in\mathcal U$ choose one epimorphism $p_U:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_U}\to\mathcal F|_U$ among these. Let $\mathcal K_U=\operatorname{Ker}(p_U)$, $\mathcal K_U(W)=\ker(p_U(W))$, a sub-$\mathcal O_U$-module of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_U}$ which is the kernel of $p_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The complex $\mathcal K_U\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_U}\xrightarrow{p_U}\mathcal F|_U$ is exact at $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_U}$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (the image of the inclusion of the kernel is the kernel) and $p_U$ is an epimorphism, so $p_U$ is a cokernel of $\mathcal K_U\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r_U}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a). As $\pi_{t_U}$ is also a cokernel of that map ($t_U=(U,r_U,\mathcal K_U)\in T$), the universal properties give a unique isomorphism $\psi_U:Q_{t_U}\to\mathcal F|_U$ with $\psi_U\circ\pi_{t_U}=p_U$. Put $\varphi_{UV}=(\psi_V|_{U\cap V})^{-1}\circ\psi_U|_{U\cap V}$, an isomorphism $Q_{t_U}|_{U\cap V}\to Q_{t_V}|_{U\cap V}$; on $U\cap V\cap W$, $\varphi_{VW}\circ\varphi_{UV}=\psi_W^{-1}\psi_V\psi_V^{-1}\psi_U=\psi_W^{-1}\psi_U=\varphi_{UW}$ (restrictions understood, restriction being compatible with composition), so the cocycle condition holds and $d_{\mathcal F}=(\mathcal U,(r_U,\mathcal K_U),(\varphi_{UV}))\in D$.

Every finite type module is some $\Phi(d)$ up to isomorphism. With $d=d_{\mathcal F}$ of Step 4 and $\theta_U=\theta^d_U$ of Step 3, put $\chi_U=\psi_U\circ\theta_U:\Phi(d)|_U\to\mathcal F|_U$, an isomorphism. On $U\cap V$: $\chi_V=\psi_V\theta_V=\psi_V\varphi_{UV}\theta_U=\psi_V\psi_V^{-1}\psi_U\theta_U=\chi_U$ (restrictions understood). By [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1) the $\chi_U$ glue to $\chi:\Phi(d)\to\mathcal F$ with $\chi|_U=\chi_U$, and likewise the inverses $\chi_U^{-1}$, which also agree on overlaps, glue to $\chi':\mathcal F\to\Phi(d)$. Then $(\chi'\chi)|_U=\chi_U^{-1}\chi_U=\mathrm{id}$ and $(\chi\chi')|_U=\mathrm{id}$ for every $U\in\mathcal U$, so by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1) $\chi'\chi=\mathrm{id}$ and $\chi\chi'=\mathrm{id}$: $\mathcal F\cong\Phi(d_{\mathcal F})$.

proof.text: Conclusion. Let $I=\{d\in D:\Phi(d)\text{ is of finite presentation}\}$, a subset of the set $D$ (Step 2), and $\mathcal G_d=\Phi(d)$ for $d\in I$. If $\mathcal G$ is any $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation, it is of finite type by Step 1 (i), so $\mathcal G\cong\Phi(d_{\mathcal G})$ by Steps 4 and 5, and then $\Phi(d_{\mathcal G})$ is of finite presentation by Step 1 (ii); hence $d_{\mathcal G}\in I$ and $\mathcal G\cong\mathcal G_{d_{\mathcal G}}$. (Stacks further picks one element per isomorphism class to get 'exactly one'; the statement here does not need it.)
